name: Clocks resolve the gravitational redshift
summary: Optical lattice and ion clocks at 1e-18 measure the GR redshift over cm (now sub-mm) heights, turning a classic GR test into a table-top AMO measurement and enabling chronometric geodesy.
sources: Chou et al. (2010). "Optical Clocks and Relativity". *Science* 329, 1630. [doi:10.1126/science.1192720](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1192720)
Bothwell et al. (2022). "Resolving the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample". *Nature* 602, 420. [arXiv:2109.12238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.12238)
Ludlow et al. (2015). "Optical atomic clocks". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 637. [arXiv:1407.3493](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.3493)

name: Quantum tests of the equivalence principle
summary: Matter-wave interferometry tests free-fall universality and gravitational phase shifts with quantum probes: the COW neutron experiment, then dual-species atom interferometers comparing isotopes.
sources: Colella, Overhauser & Werner (1975). "Observation of Gravitationally Induced Quantum Interference". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 34, 1472. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472)
Dimopoulos et al. (2007). "Testing General Relativity with Atom Interferometry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 111102. [arXiv:gr-qc/0610047](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0610047)

name: Clock comparisons as Lorentz-symmetry tests
summary: Ion and lattice clocks and entangled ion pairs bound Standard-Model-Extension coefficients through sidereal modulation of transition frequencies; clock pairs also measured time dilation at m/s speeds.
sources: Sanner et al. (2019). "Optical clock comparison for Lorentz symmetry testing". *Nature* 567, 204. [doi:10.1038/s41586-019-0972-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-0972-2)
Pruttivarasin et al. (2015). "Michelson–Morley analogue for electrons using trapped ions to test Lorentz symmetry". *Nature* 517, 592. [doi:10.1038/nature14091](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14091)
Kostelecký & Russell (2011). "Data tables for Lorentz and CPT violation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 11. [arXiv:0801.0287](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0287)

name: Atom interferometers and clocks as GW detectors
summary: Proposed mid-band (0.01-10 Hz) detectors replace laser arms by light-pulse atom interferometry or clock comparisons between distant ensembles, using single-photon transitions to cancel laser phase noise.
sources: Graham et al. (2013). "New Method for Gravitational Wave Detection with Atomic Sensors". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 110, 171102. [arXiv:1206.0818](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.0818)
Kolkowitz et al. (2016). "Gravitational wave detection with optical lattice atomic clocks". *Phys. Rev. D* 94, 124043. [arXiv:1606.01859](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01859)

name: Atomic time underlies pulsar timing
summary: Pulsar arrival times are referenced to atomic time; clock-standard errors appear as a monopolar correlated residual distinct from the quadrupolar Hellings-Downs signature, and pulsar ensembles can cross-check atomic time scales.
sources: Hobbs et al. (2012). "Development of a pulsar-based time-scale". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 427, 2780. [arXiv:1208.3560](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.3560)

name: Black-hole evaporation as an open quantum system
summary: Treating hole plus radiation as a bipartite quantum system lets open-system and entropy tools (reduced density matrices, Renyi entropies, replica trick) diagnose unitarity; the Page curve is the radiation's entanglement entropy.
sources: Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

Almheiri, Engelhardt, Marolf & Maxfield (2019). "The entropy of bulk quantum fields and the entanglement wedge of an evaporating black hole". *JHEP* 12, 063. [arXiv:1905.08762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08762)

name: Black holes as fastest scramblers
summary: Black holes scramble information in a time ~ (beta/2pi) ln S and saturate the Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford bound on the OTOC Lyapunov exponent; Hayden-Preskill shows information thrown in after the Page time re-emerges after one scrambling time.
sources: Maldacena, Shenker & Stanford (2016). "A bound on chaos". *JHEP* 08, 106. [arXiv:1503.01409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01409)
Hayden & Preskill (2007). "Black holes as mirrors: quantum information in random subsystems". *JHEP* 09, 120. [arXiv:0708.4025](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.4025)
Sekino & Susskind (2008). "Fast Scramblers". *JHEP* 10, 065. [arXiv:0808.2096](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2096)

name: SYK model and near-AdS2 gravity
summary: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model of N Majoranas with random all-to-all couplings is maximally chaotic, and its low-energy Schwarzian sector matches Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity in near-AdS2: a solvable bridge between quantum chaos and holography.
sources: Maldacena & Stanford (2016). "Remarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model". *Phys. Rev. D* 94, 106002. [arXiv:1604.07818](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07818)
Sachdev & Ye (1993). "Gapless spin-fluid ground state in a random quantum Heisenberg magnet". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 3339. [arXiv:cond-mat/9212030](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9212030)

name: Ryu-Takayanagi: entanglement equals area
summary: Boundary entanglement entropy of a region equals the minimal bulk surface area in Planck units; entanglement builds connected spacetime, and MERA tensor networks give a discrete toy bulk.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)
Van Raamsdonk (2010). "Building up spacetime with quantum entanglement". *Gen. Rel. Grav.* 42, 2323. [arXiv:1005.3035](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3035)
Swingle (2012). "Entanglement Renormalization and Holography". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 065007. [arXiv:0905.1317](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1317)

name: Holographic codes: bulk locality as QEC
summary: Bulk operators in AdS/CFT can be reconstructed on many boundary subregions, exactly as logical operators of an erasure-correcting code; perfect-tensor (HaPPY) codes reproduce RT and entanglement-wedge reconstruction.
map: \mathcal H_{\rm bulk}\hookrightarrow\mathcal H_{\rm code}\subset\mathcal H_{\rm CFT};\ \text{RT}\leftrightarrow\text{min-cut}
sources: Almheiri, Dong & Harlow (2015). "Bulk Locality and Quantum Error Correction in AdS/CFT". *JHEP* 04, 163. [arXiv:1411.7041](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7041)

Pastawski, Yoshida, Harlow & Preskill (2015). "Holographic quantum error-correcting codes: Toy models for the bulk/boundary correspondence". *JHEP* 06, 149. [arXiv:1503.06237](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06237)

name: Page curve, monogamy and the firewall
summary: Page's typical-subsystem entropy gives the rise and fall of radiation entropy; monogamy of entanglement forbids late Hawking modes being maximally entangled with both early radiation and interior partners (the AMPS firewall).
sources: Page (1993). "Average entropy of a subsystem". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 1291. [arXiv:gr-qc/9305007](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9305007)
Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Almheiri, Marolf, Polchinski & Sully (2013). "Black Holes: Complementarity or Firewalls?". *JHEP* 02, 062. [arXiv:1207.3123](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.3123)

name: Entanglement area law and black-hole entropy
summary: Tracing out field modes inside a surface gives an entanglement entropy proportional to its area with a cutoff-dependent coefficient, a candidate microscopic contribution to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.
sources: Srednicki (1993). "Entropy and area". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 666. [arXiv:hep-th/9303048](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9303048)
Bombelli, Koul, Lee & Sorkin (1986). "Quantum source of entropy for black holes". *Phys. Rev. D* 34, 373. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.34.373](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.34.373)

name: Gravity-mediated entanglement witness (BMV)
summary: LOCC cannot create entanglement, so if two masses in superposition become entangled through gravity alone, gravity cannot act as a classical channel; the proposed test is a direct application of entanglement monotonicity.
sources: Bose et al. (2017). "Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 240401. [arXiv:1707.06050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06050)

Marletto & Vedral (2017). "Gravitationally-induced entanglement between two massive particles is sufficient evidence of quantum effects in gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 240402. [arXiv:1707.06036](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06036)

name: Quantum foundations meets quantum gravity
summary: Tabletop tests of the quantum nature of gravity (gravity-induced entanglement, gravitational collapse) grew out of foundations research and tie the measurement problem to the quantum status of spacetime.
sources: Bose et al. (2017). "Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 240401. [arXiv:1707.06050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06050)
Penrose (1996). "On Gravity's role in Quantum State Reduction". *Gen. Rel. Grav.* 28, 581. [doi:10.1007/BF02105068](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02105068)

name: Gravitational objective collapse (Penrose-Diosi)
summary: Superpositions of distinct mass distributions are proposed to collapse at a rate set by the gravitational self-energy of their difference: a dynamical answer to the measurement problem, testable with massive superpositions.
sources: Penrose (1996). "On Gravity's role in Quantum State Reduction". *Gen. Rel. Grav.* 28, 581. [doi:10.1007/BF02105068](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02105068)
Diósi (1989). "Models for universal reduction of macroscopic quantum fluctuations". *Phys. Rev. A* 40, 1165. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.40.1165](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.40.1165)

name: Proper-time which-path decoherence
summary: A clock in superposition at two heights records which-path proper time, so interferometric visibility drops; gravitational time dilation gives a universal decoherence for composite systems with internal dynamics.
sources: Zych, Costa, Pikovski & Brukner (2011). "Quantum interferometric visibility as a witness of general relativistic proper time". *Nat. Commun.* 2, 505. [arXiv:1105.4531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.4531)
Pikovski, Zych, Costa & Brukner (2015). "Universal decoherence due to gravitational time dilation". *Nature Phys.* 11, 668. [arXiv:1311.1095](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1095)

name: Optomechanical probes of Planck-scale physics
summary: Quantum-optical control of massive oscillators can bound deformed canonical commutators (minimal-length models) and test gravity-related collapse in macroscopic superpositions.
sources: Pikovski et al. (2012). "Probing Planck-scale physics with quantum optics". *Nature Phys.* 8, 393. [arXiv:1111.1979](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.1979)

name: LIGO mirrors as optomechanical systems
summary: Interferometer test masses are radiation-pressure-coupled oscillators: optical springs, parametric instabilities, ponderomotive squeezing and feedback cooling of 10 kg mirrors toward the motional ground state are cavity optomechanics at kg scale.
sources: Whittle et al. (2021). "Approaching the motional ground state of a 10-kg object". *Science* 372, 1333. [arXiv:2102.12665](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.12665)
Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Squeezed-light injection in GW detectors
summary: Injecting squeezed vacuum into the dark port lowers shot noise below the standard quantum limit; frequency-dependent squeezing also cuts radiation-pressure noise. Used in LIGO and Virgo observing runs since 2019.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)
LIGO Scientific Collaboration (2011). "A gravitational wave observatory operating beyond the quantum shot-noise limit". *Nature Phys.* 7, 962. [arXiv:1109.2295](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.2295)

Tse et al. (2019). "Quantum-Enhanced Advanced LIGO Detectors in the Era of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 123, 231107. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.231107](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.231107)

name: Standard quantum limit of interferometry
summary: A GW interferometer is a quantum-optical measurement whose sensitivity is set by the trade-off between photon shot noise and radiation-pressure back-action, the standard quantum limit.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)

name: Quantum metrology for GW astronomy
summary: Gravitational-wave science drives squeezing at audio frequencies and filter-cavity development; the detectors are the most sensitive deployed quantum-enhanced instruments.
sources: Tse et al. (2019). "Quantum-Enhanced Advanced LIGO Detectors in the Era of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 123, 231107. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.231107](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.231107)

name: Unruh/Hawking vacuum as two-mode squeezing
summary: The Bogoliubov transformation between Minkowski and Rindler (or in and out) modes is exactly a two-mode squeezing operator; the Minkowski vacuum is a two-mode squeezed state across the horizon, thermal on either side.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)
Crispino, Higuchi & Matsas (2008). "The Unruh effect and its applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 787. [arXiv:0710.5373](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5373)

name: Dynamical Casimir effect in circuit QED
summary: Modulating a superconducting resonator's boundary condition with a SQUID at GHz rates creates photon pairs from vacuum, the same parametric particle creation as moving mirrors and cosmological particle production.
sources: Wilson et al. (2011). "Observation of the dynamical Casimir effect in a superconducting circuit". *Nature* 479, 376. [arXiv:1105.4714](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.4714)

name: Unruh-DeWitt detector is a two-level atom
summary: The detector used to define Unruh and Hawking radiation is a two-level system coupled to a quantum field, the atom-field model of quantum optics; accelerated detectors see thermal photon statistics.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)
Crispino, Higuchi & Matsas (2008). "The Unruh effect and its applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 787. [arXiv:0710.5373](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5373)

name: Acoustic horizons and analogue Hawking radiation
summary: Bogoliubov phonons in a flowing BEC propagate on an acoustic metric; where flow exceeds sound speed a horizon forms and thermal, entangled phonon pairs are emitted. Curated in the analogue-gravity theme.
breaks: Kinematics only: no Einstein dynamics or backreaction; Bogoliubov dispersion breaks Lorentz invariance at the healing length; nK signals sit on thermal noise.
sources: Unruh (1981). "Experimental Black-Hole Evaporation?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 46, 1351. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351)
Barceló, Liberati & Visser (2005). "Analogue Gravity". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 12. [arXiv:gr-qc/0505065](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0505065)
Steinhauer (2016). "Observation of quantum Hawking radiation and its entanglement in an analogue black hole". *Nature Phys.* 12, 959. [arXiv:1510.00621](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00621)

name: BEC simulators of cosmological particle creation
summary: Rapidly expanding ring BECs and modulated condensates emulate particle creation in expanding spacetimes and Unruh radiation, testing QFT-in-curved-spacetime kinematics with phonons.
breaks: Effective metric only; condensate dissipation and nonlinearity have no curved-spacetime counterpart.
sources: Eckel et al. (2018). "A Rapidly Expanding Bose-Einstein Condensate: An Expanding Universe in the Lab". *Phys. Rev. X* 8, 021021. [arXiv:1710.05800](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05800)
Hu et al. (2019). "Quantum simulation of Unruh radiation". *Nature Phys.* 15, 785. [arXiv:1807.07504](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.07504)

name: Bekenstein bound from relative entropy
summary: Quantum-information thermodynamics (positivity of relative entropy) gives a precise statement and proof of the Bekenstein bound and underpins the generalized second law.
sources: Casini (2008). "Relative entropy and the Bekenstein bound". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 25, 205021. [arXiv:0804.2182](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.2182)

name: Euclidean path integral gives the Hawking temperature
summary: Wick-rotating the black-hole metric and demanding regularity at the horizon forces periodic imaginary time, identical to the thermal path-integral period; the Euclidean action gives the partition function and entropy.
sources: Gibbons & Hawking (1977). "Action integrals and partition functions in quantum gravity". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2752. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752)

name: No-boundary wavefunction of the universe
summary: Hartle and Hawking define the state of the universe as a Euclidean path integral over compact geometries, transplanting semiclassical and instanton machinery from QM to quantum cosmology.
sources: Hartle & Hawking (1983). "Wave function of the Universe". *Phys. Rev. D* 28, 2960. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960)

name: Hawking radiation as WKB tunnelling
summary: The emission rate can be computed as a semiclassical tunnelling probability across the horizon; energy conservation gives small non-thermal corrections.
sources: Parikh & Wilczek (2000). "Hawking radiation as tunneling". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 85, 5042. [arXiv:hep-th/9907001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9907001)

name: Poschl-Teller and WKB models of ringdown
summary: Black-hole perturbations obey a Schrodinger-like Regge-Wheeler/Zerilli equation; replacing the barrier by an exactly solvable Poschl-Teller potential, or expanding it by WKB, gives the quasinormal ringdown frequencies.
sources: Ferrari & Mashhoon (1984). "New approach to the quasinormal modes of a black hole". *Phys. Rev. D* 30, 295. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.30.295](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.30.295)
Schutz & Will (1985). "Black hole normal modes: a semianalytic approach". *Astrophys. J.* 291, L33. [doi:10.1086/184453](https://doi.org/10.1086/184453)

name: Quasinormal modes as non-Hermitian spectra
summary: Outgoing boundary conditions make the black-hole perturbation operator non-self-adjoint; quasinormal modes are resonances whose pseudospectrum shows the spectral instability familiar from non-Hermitian physics.
sources: Jaramillo, Panosso Macedo & Al Sheikh (2021). "Pseudospectrum and Black Hole Quasinormal Mode Instability". *Phys. Rev. X* 11, 031003. [arXiv:2004.06434](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.06434)

name: Black-hole scattering and partial waves
summary: Wave scattering off Schwarzschild and Kerr holes uses partial-wave phase shifts, greybody factors and absorption cross sections from quantum scattering theory; rotating holes superradiantly amplify modes with omega < m Omega_H.

name: SU(2) recoupling builds spin networks
summary: Loop quantum gravity labels spin-network edges by SU(2) irreps and nodes by intertwiners; the area spectrum is the SU(2) Casimir and spin-foam amplitudes use 6j symbols from angular-momentum recoupling.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1995). "Discreteness of area and volume in quantum gravity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 442, 593. [arXiv:gr-qc/9411005](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9411005)

name: Spinors, Lorentz group and Thomas precession
summary: Spin-1/2 is a representation of SL(2,C), the double cover of the Lorentz group; Thomas precession (a Wigner rotation) supplies the factor 1/2 in atomic spin-orbit coupling, and the Dirac equation gives g=2 and fine structure.
sources: Thomas (1926). "The Motion of the Spinning Electron". *Nature* 117, 514. [doi:10.1038/117514a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/117514a0)
Dirac (1928). "The quantum theory of the electron". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 117, 610. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1928.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1928.0023)

name: Bell tests need spacelike separation
summary: Bell's local causality is defined by light cones; loophole-free tests choose settings and record outcomes at spacelike separation, and no-signalling keeps quantum nonlocality compatible with relativity.
sources: Aspect, Dalibard & Roger (1982). "Experimental Test of Bell's Inequalities Using Time-Varying Analyzers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 1804. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1804](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1804)
Hensen et al. (2015). "Loophole-free Bell inequality violation using electron spins separated by 1.3 kilometres". *Nature* 526, 682. [arXiv:1508.05949](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05949)

name: Berry connection vs Levi-Civita connection
summary: The Berry phase is the holonomy of a U(1) connection on parameter space, as a vector's rotation after parallel transport is the holonomy of the Levi-Civita connection; both are connections with curvature on fibre bundles.
breaks: Berry curvature is a non-dynamical abelian field on Hilbert-space parameters; spacetime curvature is a dynamical SO(3,1) connection fixed by Einstein's equations.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

name: Gravitational Aharonov-Bohm effect
summary: Atom interferometers measured a gravitational phase shift on wavepackets that feel no net gravitational force, the gravitational counterpart of the Aharonov-Bohm effect.
sources: Overstreet et al. (2022). "Observation of a gravitational Aharonov-Bohm effect". *Science* 375, 226. [doi:10.1126/science.abl7152](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abl7152)

name: Holographic complexity
summary: Quantum circuit complexity is conjectured to be dual to the growing volume or action of the black-hole interior (complexity = volume or action).
sources: Susskind (2016). "Computational complexity and black hole horizons". *Fortsch. Phys.* 64, 24. [arXiv:1403.5695](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5695)
Brown et al. (2016). "Holographic Complexity Equals Bulk Action?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 191301. [arXiv:1509.07876](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.07876)

name: Wormhole teleportation on quantum processors
summary: Quantum processors have emulated SYK-like teleportation protocols interpreted as traversable wormholes; the 2022 superconducting-processor claim is contested because the learned Hamiltonian may not be holographic.
sources: Jafferis et al. (2022). "Traversable wormhole dynamics on a quantum processor". *Nature* 612, 51. [doi:10.1038/s41586-022-05424-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05424-3)

name: Problem of time and relational evolution
summary: Canonical quantum gravity imposes the Wheeler-DeWitt constraint H|Psi>=0, so there is no external time; the Page-Wootters mechanism recovers Schrodinger dynamics as correlations between a clock subsystem and the rest.
sources: DeWitt (1967). "Quantum Theory of Gravity. I. The Canonical Theory". *Phys. Rev.* 160, 1113. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.160.1113](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.160.1113)
Page & Wootters (1983). "Evolution without evolution: Dynamics described by stationary observables". *Phys. Rev. D* 27, 2885. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.27.2885](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.27.2885)

name: Quantum repeaters for VLBI baselines
summary: Distributing entanglement between telescopes would allow optical interferometry with arbitrarily long baselines without transporting photons, a possible extension of EHT-style imaging to optical wavelengths.
sources: Gottesman, Jennewein & Croke (2012). "Longer-Baseline Telescopes Using Quantum Repeaters". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 109, 070503. [arXiv:1107.2939](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.2939)

name: Electron EDM in polar molecules
summary: Polar molecules (ThO, HfF+) amplify a lab field into internal effective fields of 10-100 GV/cm; spin-precession measurements bound the electron EDM below 1e-29 e cm, probing CP-violating physics at multi-TeV scales.
sources: ACME Collaboration (2018). "Improved limit on the electric dipole moment of the electron". *Nature* 562, 355. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8)
Roussy et al. (2023). "An improved bound on the electron's electric dipole moment". *Science* 381, 46. [doi:10.1126/science.adg4084](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adg4084)

name: Second quantization: QM of many particles is QFT
summary: Non-relativistic many-body quantum mechanics in Fock space is a free or interacting quantum field theory; relativistic QFT adds Lorentz invariance, antiparticles and particle number non-conservation.

name: Feynman path integral from particles to fields
summary: The QFT generating functional is the particle path integral with paths replaced by field configurations; stationary phase gives the classical field equations and Gaussian integrals give propagators and Wick's theorem.
sources: Feynman (1948). "Space-Time Approach to Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 20, 367. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367)

name: Born series as tree-level perturbation theory
summary: The Lippmann-Schwinger Born series is the non-relativistic limit of the Feynman-diagram expansion: first Born approximation equals tree-level one-boson exchange (Yukawa/Coulomb), and the optical theorem is S-matrix unitarity.
map: f_{\rm Born}=-\frac{m}{2\pi\hbar^2}\tilde V(\mathbf q)\leftrightarrow\mathcal M\propto\frac{g^2}{q^2+m^2};\ \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}\mathrm{Im}f(0)

name: Wave-packet decoherence of neutrino oscillations
summary: Mass eigenstates in a neutrino wave packet separate over a coherence length, damping oscillations exactly as which-path information kills interference; open-system (Lindblad) models also bound exotic decoherence from new physics.
sources: Akhmedov & Smirnov (2009). "Paradoxes of neutrino oscillations". *Phys. Atom. Nucl.* 72, 1363. [arXiv:0905.1903](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1903)

name: MSW conversion as an adiabatic level crossing
summary: Resonant flavour conversion in the Sun is an avoided crossing of matter-dressed mass eigenstates; adiabatic following gives near-complete conversion and the non-adiabatic hopping probability is the Landau-Zener formula.
sources: Parke (1986). "Nonadiabatic Level Crossing in Resonant Neutrino Oscillations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 1275. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1275](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1275)
Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: Neutrino flavour as a precessing pseudo-spin
summary: Two-flavour oscillation is spin-1/2 precession in an effective magnetic field; the oscillation formula is the Rabi formula, and collective oscillations in dense neutrino gases map onto interacting spin models.

name: Leggett-Garg violation in neutrino oscillations
summary: Temporal (Leggett-Garg) inequalities, the time-domain analogue of Bell tests, are violated by MINOS oscillation data, showing neutrino flavour evolution is incompatible with macrorealism over 735 km.
sources: Formaggio et al. (2016). "Violation of the Leggett-Garg Inequality in Neutrino Oscillations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 117, 050402. [arXiv:1602.00041](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.00041)

name: Clocks search for ultralight dark matter
summary: Ultralight scalar dark matter would make fundamental constants oscillate; comparing clocks with different sensitivity to alpha and m_e/m_p detects such oscillations at frequencies set by the DM mass.
sources: Arvanitaki, Huang & Van Tilburg (2015). "Searching for dilaton dark matter with atomic clocks". *Phys. Rev. D* 91, 015015. [arXiv:1405.2925](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2925)

name: Isotope-shift King plots probe new bosons
summary: A new light boson coupling electrons to neutrons would bend the King plot of isotope shifts; precision ion spectroscopy constrains such Yukawa forces at keV-MeV masses.
sources: Berengut et al. (2018). "Probing New Long-Range Interactions by Isotope Shift Spectroscopy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 091801. [arXiv:1704.05068](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.05068)

name: Squeezed-state receivers for axion haloscopes
summary: Haloscopes convert axions to microwave photons in a resonant cavity; HAYSTAC injected squeezed vacuum to beat the quantum limit on scan rate, a direct import of quantum metrology.
sources: Backes et al. (2021). "A quantum enhanced search for dark matter axions". *Nature* 590, 238. [arXiv:2008.01853](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01853)

name: Qubit photon counting for dark-photon searches
summary: A transmon dispersively coupled to a cavity counts photons by repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, evading the standard quantum limit of linear amplifiers in hidden-photon and axion searches.
sources: Dixit et al. (2021). "Searching for Dark Matter with a Superconducting Qubit". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 126, 141302. [arXiv:2008.12231](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.12231)

name: Electron g-2 and alpha test QED
summary: A single-electron Penning-trap measurement of g/2 and atom-recoil measurements of alpha (Cs, Rb) test QED at the 1e-13 level; their mutual tension is part of the lepton g-2 anomaly landscape.
sources: Fan et al. (2023). "Measurement of the Electron Magnetic Moment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 130, 071801. [arXiv:2209.13084](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.13084)
Parker et al. (2018). "Measurement of the fine-structure constant as a test of the Standard Model". *Science* 360, 191. [arXiv:1812.04130](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04130)

Morel et al. (2020). "Determination of the fine-structure constant with an accuracy of 81 parts per trillion". *Nature* 588, 61. [doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7)

name: Lamb shift and the birth of renormalization
summary: The 1947 Lamb shift measurement and Bethe's mass-renormalized calculation launched renormalized QED; hydrogen spectroscopy remains a precision test of bound-state QED.
sources: Lamb & Retherford (1947). "Fine Structure of the Hydrogen Atom by a Microwave Method". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 241. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.241](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.241)
Bethe (1947). "The Electromagnetic Shift of Energy Levels". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 339. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.339](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.339)

name: Atomic parity violation measures the weak charge
summary: Z exchange between electrons and the nucleus mixes S and P states; the Cs 6S-7S parity-violating amplitude gives the nuclear weak charge and sin^2 theta_W at low momentum transfer, complementary to colliders.
sources: Wood et al. (1997). "Measurement of Parity Nonconservation and an Anapole Moment in Cesium". *Science* 275, 1759. [doi:10.1126/science.275.5307.1759](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.275.5307.1759)

name: Entanglement of top-quark pairs at the LHC
summary: Top-antitop spin correlations reconstructed from decay leptons are a two-qubit density matrix; ATLAS and CMS observed entanglement near threshold using quantum-information witnesses.
sources: ATLAS Collaboration (2024). "Observation of quantum entanglement with top quarks at the ATLAS detector". *Nature* 633, 542. [arXiv:2311.07288](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07288)
Barr et al. (2024). "Quantum entanglement and Bell inequality violation at colliders". [arXiv:2402.07972](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07972)

name: Entangled neutral mesons and Bell tests
summary: Pairs of neutral K or B mesons from phi or Upsilon(4S) decays are produced in flavour-entangled EPR states, used to time-tag CP and flavour measurements and to test Bell-type inequalities with decaying systems.
breaks: Decay and lack of free measurement-setting choice prevent loophole-free Bell tests.
sources: Barr et al. (2024). "Quantum entanglement and Bell inequality violation at colliders". [arXiv:2402.07972](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07972)

name: Kaon mixing is a non-Hermitian two-level system
summary: The Weisskopf-Wigner effective Hamiltonian of neutral kaons (or B mesons) is the non-Hermitian matrix M - i Gamma/2; its non-orthogonal eigenstates K_S, K_L and their overlap encode CP violation.
sources: Lee, Oehme & Yang (1957). "Remarks on Possible Noninvariance under Time Reversal and Charge Conjugation". *Phys. Rev.* 106, 340. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.106.340](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.106.340)

name: Analog quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories
summary: Cold atoms and Rydberg arrays implement Hamiltonian lattice gauge theories with Gauss's law enforced by energy penalties or constraints, accessing real-time dynamics and finite density where Euclidean Monte Carlo has a sign problem.
sources: Bañuls et al. (2020). "Simulating lattice gauge theories within quantum technologies". *Eur. Phys. J. D* 74, 165. [arXiv:1911.00003](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00003)

name: Digital quantum algorithms for QFT
summary: Hamiltonian-simulation algorithms compute scattering in scalar and gauge field theories in polynomial time, a route around the sign problem of lattice QCD at finite density and real time.
sources: Jordan, Lee & Preskill (2012). "Quantum Algorithms for Quantum Field Theories". *Science* 336, 1130. [arXiv:1111.3633](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3633)

name: Trapped-ion simulation of the Schwinger model
summary: A few trapped-ion qubits simulated real-time pair creation in 1+1D QED after eliminating the gauge field; circuit-QED and tensor-network studies extend this to meson scattering.
sources: Martinez et al. (2016). "Real-time dynamics of lattice gauge theories with a few-qubit quantum computer". *Nature* 534, 516. [arXiv:1605.04570](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04570)
Belyansky et al. (2024). "High-Energy Collision of Quarks and Mesons in the Schwinger Model: From Tensor Networks to Circuit QED". [arXiv:2307.02522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02522)

name: Entanglement entropy measures the central charge
summary: In a 1+1D CFT the entanglement entropy of an interval grows logarithmically with a coefficient fixed by the central charge, so entanglement diagnoses criticality and universality classes.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2004). "Entanglement entropy and quantum field theory". *J. Stat. Mech.* 0406, P06002. [arXiv:hep-th/0405152](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405152)
Holzhey, Larsen & Wilczek (1994). "Geometric and renormalized entropy in conformal field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 424, 443. [arXiv:hep-th/9403108](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9403108)

name: Instantons from double wells to QCD
summary: Euclidean instantons that compute tunnelling splitting in a double well become Yang-Mills instantons, which break U(1)_A through the anomaly and mix the theta vacua.
sources: 't Hooft (1976). "Symmetry Breaking through Bell-Jackiw Anomalies". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 37, 8. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.8](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.8)

name: Theta vacua as Bloch states; WZ terms as Berry phases
summary: Large gauge transformations make the Yang-Mills vacuum periodic, and theta plays the role of Bloch quasi-momentum in a periodic potential; Wess-Zumino-Witten terms are Berry phases of the low-energy fields.
sources: Jackiw & Rebbi (1976). "Vacuum Periodicity in a Yang-Mills Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 37, 172. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.172](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.172)

name: Wilson loops are non-abelian holonomies
summary: The Aharonov-Bohm phase is a U(1) holonomy; Yang-Mills Wilson loops are its non-abelian generalization, and degenerate adiabatic transport produces the same Wilczek-Zee non-abelian connection.
sources: Aharonov & Bohm (1959). "Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev.* 115, 485. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.115.485](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.115.485)
Wu & Yang (1975). "Concept of nonintegrable phase factors and global formulation of gauge fields". *Phys. Rev. D* 12, 3845. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845)
Wilczek & Zee (1984). "Appearance of Gauge Structure in Simple Dynamical Systems". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 2111. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111)

name: Isospin and flavour multiplets via SU(2) recoupling
summary: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and the Wigner-Eckart theorem developed for angular momentum organize isospin and flavour multiplets, decay branching ratios and helicity amplitudes of hadrons.

name: Quarkonium as hydrogen of QCD
summary: Charmonium and bottomonium spectra follow from a Schrodinger equation with a Coulomb-plus-linear (Cornell) potential, organized like hydrogen and positronium levels with fine and hyperfine splittings.
breaks: Confinement (linear term) has no atomic analogue; relativistic corrections and coupled open-flavour channels matter above threshold.
sources: Eichten et al. (1975). "Spectrum of Charmed Quark-Antiquark Bound States". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 34, 369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369)

name: Near-threshold states and universality
summary: Hadrons near a two-body threshold (deuteron, X(3872)) are governed by a large scattering length, the same universal physics as Feshbach-tuned cold atoms, including Efimov-type three-body effects.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)

name: Higgs amplitude mode in superfluids
summary: Near the superfluid-Mott transition, optical-lattice bosons have a gapped amplitude ('Higgs') mode of the order parameter, observed by lattice modulation spectroscopy.
breaks: No gauge field, so no Higgs mechanism; the amplitude mode can decay into Goldstone pairs and is only well defined near Lorentz-invariant criticality.
sources: Endres et al. (2012). "The 'Higgs' amplitude mode at the two-dimensional superfluid/Mott insulator transition". *Nature* 487, 454. [arXiv:1204.5183](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.5183)

name: Schrieffer-Wolff elimination as integrating out
summary: Adiabatic elimination of high-energy states by second-order perturbation theory (Schrieffer-Wolff) gives effective Hamiltonians, the same logic as integrating out heavy fields; Fermi's four-fermion coupling is W exchange at second order.

name: Golden rule and decay widths
summary: Fermi's golden rule is the non-relativistic form of the relativistic decay-rate and cross-section formulas built from Feynman amplitudes and Lorentz-invariant phase space.

name: Supersymmetric quantum mechanics
summary: Witten introduced SUSY QM as a toy model of supersymmetry breaking (Witten index); it became a tool for exactly solvable potentials through shape invariance and partner Hamiltonians.
sources: Witten (1981). "Dynamical breaking of supersymmetry". *Nucl. Phys. B* 188, 513. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(81)90006-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90006-7)
Cooper, Khare & Sukhatme (1995). "Supersymmetry and quantum mechanics". *Phys. Rep.* 251, 267. [arXiv:hep-th/9405029](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9405029)

name: Quantized EM field as free QFT
summary: Quantum optics' mode expansion of the field, Fock and coherent states are the canonical quantization of free Maxwell theory; Glauber coherent states are the quantum states closest to classical fields.
sources: Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)

name: Single-photon detectors in particle detectors
summary: Calorimeters, Cherenkov and scintillator systems read out light with single-photon-sensitive devices (PMTs, SiPMs, SPAD arrays); quantum-optics detector metrics such as efficiency, dark counts and timing jitter set detector performance.

name: Quantum algorithms for parton showers
summary: Quantum circuits can simulate parton showers including quantum interference between emission histories that classical Markov showers drop.
sources: Bauer et al. (2021). "Quantum Algorithm for High Energy Physics Simulations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 126, 062001. [arXiv:1904.03196](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03196)

name: Quantum machine learning for collider data
summary: Variational quantum classifiers and kernels have been tried on jet tagging and event classification; no advantage over classical deep learning has been demonstrated.
sources: Biamonte et al. (2017). "Quantum machine learning". *Nature* 549, 195. [arXiv:1611.09347](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.09347)

name: Alpha decay as Coulomb-barrier tunnelling
summary: Gamow and Gurney-Condon explained alpha decay as tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier; the barrier-penetration factor gives the Geiger-Nuttall law spanning 20+ orders of magnitude in half-life.
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)
Gurney & Condon (1928). "Wave Mechanics and Radioactive Disintegration". *Nature* 122, 439. [doi:10.1038/122439a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/122439a0)

name: Partial waves, resonances and the optical model
summary: Nuclear reaction theory is applied quantum scattering theory: phase shifts and partial waves, Breit-Wigner compound resonances, the complex optical potential (absorption via Im V), and R-matrix fits of cross sections.

name: Coulomb wavefunctions and the Gamow factor
summary: Charged-particle reaction rates factor into a smooth astrophysical S-factor and the Sommerfeld/Gamow penetrability that comes from exact Coulomb scattering wavefunctions at the origin.

name: Proton radius from hydrogen and muonic hydrogen
summary: The finite proton size shifts S levels; muonic-hydrogen Lamb-shift spectroscopy gave r_p = 0.84 fm, 4% below earlier e-p values, and newer hydrogen spectroscopy largely agrees, resolving most of the proton-radius puzzle.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)
Bezginov et al. (2019). "A measurement of the atomic hydrogen Lamb shift and the proton charge radius". *Science* 365, 1007. [doi:10.1126/science.aau7807](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aau7807)

name: Spin-orbit coupling and magic numbers
summary: A strong nuclear spin-orbit term splits j=l+-1/2 levels and reproduces the magic numbers; jj-coupling, Clebsch-Gordan and Wigner-Eckart machinery from atomic physics then organizes shell-model states.
breaks: Same operator algebra but different physics: nuclear spin-orbit is a strong-interaction effect, ~20x larger relative to level spacing, with inverted ordering relative to atomic fine structure.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

name: Unitary Fermi gas and dilute neutron matter
summary: The neutron-neutron scattering length (-18.5 fm) far exceeds the effective range, so low-density neutron matter is close to the unitary Fermi gas realized at Feshbach resonances; the measured Bertsch parameter benchmarks neutron-star crust EOS calculations.
sources: Carlson, Chang, Pandharipande & Schmidt (2003). "Superfluid Fermi Gases with Large Scattering Length". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 91, 050401. [arXiv:physics/0303094](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0303094)
Ku et al. (2012). "Revealing the Superfluid Lambda Transition in the Universal Thermodynamics of a Unitary Fermi Gas". *Science* 335, 563. [arXiv:1110.3309](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.3309)

name: BCS pairing in nuclei and Fermi gases
summary: Odd-even mass staggering and moments of inertia reflect BCS-like pairing in finite nuclei, the same gap equation as in BEC-BCS-crossover Fermi gases, with the cold-atom crossover a tunable laboratory for the regime. See the pairing-across-scales theme.
sources: Dean & Hjorth-Jensen (2003). "Pairing in nuclear systems: from neutron stars to finite nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 607. [arXiv:nucl-th/0210033](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0210033)

name: Scissors modes in deformed nuclei and BECs
summary: The scissors mode, a counter-rotation of proton and neutron clouds discovered in deformed nuclei, was predicted and observed in anisotropic BECs as a signature of superfluid irrotational flow.
breaks: In nuclei the mode is a proton-neutron relative rotation in a finite fermion system; in a BEC it is the tilt oscillation of a single bosonic superfluid.
sources: Guéry-Odelin & Stringari (1999). "Scissors Mode and Superfluidity of a Trapped Bose-Einstein Condensed Gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 4452. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4452](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4452)

Maragò et al. (2000). "Observation of the Scissors Mode and Evidence for Superfluidity of a Trapped Bose-Einstein Condensed Gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 84, 2056. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.2056](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.2056)

name: Elliptic flow of unitary gases and the QGP
summary: Strongly interacting Fermi gases released from anisotropic traps expand elliptically like the QGP's elliptic flow; both are nearly perfect fluids with eta/s near hbar/4 pi k_B.
breaks: Non-relativistic vs relativistic hydrodynamics; scales differ by ~1e19 in temperature; the QGP has gauge degrees of freedom and a crossover, the gas has none.
sources: O'Hara et al. (2002). "Observation of a Strongly Interacting Degenerate Fermi Gas of Atoms". *Science* 298, 2179. [arXiv:cond-mat/0212463](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0212463)
Schäfer & Teaney (2009). "Nearly perfect fluidity: from cold atomic gases to hot quark gluon plasmas". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 72, 126001. [arXiv:0904.3107](https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.3107)
Cao et al. (2011). "Universal Quantum Viscosity in a Unitary Fermi Gas". *Science* 331, 58. [arXiv:1007.2625](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.2625)

name: Feshbach resonances: from nuclear reactions to cold atoms
summary: Feshbach developed closed-channel resonance theory for nuclear reactions; the same coupled-channel physics, tuned by magnetic field, became the main tool for controlling interactions in ultracold gases.
sources: Feshbach (1958). "Unified theory of nuclear reactions". *Ann. Phys.* 5, 357. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1)
Chin et al. (2010). "Feshbach resonances in ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1225. [arXiv:0812.1496](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.1496)

name: Thorium-229 nuclear clock
summary: The 8.4 eV isomer of Th-229 has been laser-excited and frequency-referenced to a Sr clock, opening a nuclear optical clock highly sensitive to variations of alpha and the strong-interaction scale.
sources: Tiedau et al. (2024). "Laser Excitation of the Th-229 Nucleus". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 182501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.182501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.182501)

Zhang et al. (2024). "Frequency ratio of the 229mTh nuclear isomeric transition and the 87Sr atomic clock". *Nature* 633, 63. [doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07839-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07839-6)

name: Laser spectroscopy of exotic-nucleus radii and moments
summary: Isotope shifts and hyperfine structure measured by collinear laser spectroscopy give charge radii, spins and moments of short-lived nuclei, revealing halos and shell evolution far from stability.
sources: Garcia Ruiz et al. (2016). "Unexpectedly large charge radii of neutron-rich calcium isotopes". *Nature Phys.* 12, 594. [arXiv:1602.07906](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.07906)

name: Penning-trap mass spectrometry
summary: Ion-trap techniques measure masses of exotic nuclei to 1e-8 or better via cyclotron frequencies, fixing separation energies, shell gaps and drip lines.
sources: Blaum (2006). "High-accuracy mass spectrometry with stored ions". *Phys. Rep.* 425, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.011)

name: Nuclear anapole moments from atomic parity violation
summary: The nuclear-spin-dependent part of Cs parity violation revealed the nuclear anapole moment, a probe of the parity-violating nucleon-nucleon (weak meson-exchange) interaction.
sources: Wood et al. (1997). "Measurement of Parity Nonconservation and an Anapole Moment in Cesium". *Science* 275, 1759. [doi:10.1126/science.275.5307.1759](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.275.5307.1759)

name: Laser spectroscopy of superheavy atoms
summary: Atom-at-a-time resonance ionization spectroscopy of nobelium measures level energies where relativistic effects reshape atomic structure, testing relativistic many-body theory and giving nuclear moments.
sources: Laatiaoui et al. (2016). "Atom-at-a-time laser resonance ionization spectroscopy of nobelium". *Nature* 538, 495. [doi:10.1038/nature19345](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature19345)

name: Multipole selection rules for atomic and nuclear photons
summary: Gamma transitions in nuclei obey the same multipole selection rules and Wigner-Eckart structure as atomic E1/M1/E2 lines; Weisskopf estimates and conversion electrons parallel atomic radiative and Auger channels.

name: Quantum computing of nuclear ground states
summary: Variational quantum eigensolvers computed the deuteron binding energy from pionless/chiral EFT Hamiltonians on cloud processors, a first step toward quantum simulation of nuclear many-body problems.
sources: Dumitrescu et al. (2018). "Cloud Quantum Computing of an Atomic Nucleus". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 210501. [arXiv:1801.03897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.03897)

name: Random-matrix theory began with nuclear resonances
summary: Wigner and Dyson introduced random matrices to model neutron-resonance spacings in heavy nuclei; the nuclear data ensemble later anchored the Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit link between classical chaos and Wigner-Dyson statistics.
sources: Wigner (1955). "Characteristic Vectors of Bordered Matrices With Infinite Dimensions". *Ann. Math.* 62, 548. [doi:10.2307/1970079](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970079)
Dyson (1962). "Statistical Theory of the Energy Levels of Complex Systems. I". *J. Math. Phys.* 3, 140. [doi:10.1063/1.1703773](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1703773)

Bohigas, Giannoni & Schmit (1984). "Characterization of Chaotic Quantum Spectra and Universality of Level Fluctuation Laws". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 1. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1)

name: Compound nucleus as a thermalizing system
summary: Bohr's compound nucleus forgets how it was formed and decays statistically, an early instance of an isolated many-body quantum system thermalizing; Hauser-Feshbach and evaporation theory use nuclear temperature.
sources: Bohr (1936). "Neutron Capture and Nuclear Constitution". *Nature* 137, 344. [doi:10.1038/137344a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/137344a0)

name: Thermalization of an isolated QCD system
summary: Heavy-ion collisions pose the isolated-system thermalization problem at strong coupling: how a far-from-equilibrium gluon state reaches hydrodynamic behaviour in ~1 fm/c, with links to prethermalization and non-thermal fixed points studied in cold atoms.
sources: Berges, Heller, Mazeliauskas & Venugopalan (2021). "QCD thermalization: Ab initio approaches and interdisciplinary connections". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 93, 035003. [arXiv:2005.12299](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12299)

name: Quarkonium in the QGP as an open quantum system
summary: Heavy quark-antiquark pairs coupled to the QGP bath obey Lindblad equations derived from pNRQCD, describing screening, dissociation and regeneration of quarkonia beyond rate equations.
sources: Brambilla, Escobedo, Soto & Vairo (2017). "Quarkonium suppression in heavy-ion collisions: an open quantum system approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 034021. [arXiv:1612.07248](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07248)

name: WKB tunnelling and the Gamow peak
summary: Thermonuclear fusion proceeds by WKB tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier; the product of Maxwell-Boltzmann tail and penetrability gives the Gamow peak that sets stellar and fusion-reactor rates.

name: Least-action paths for spontaneous fission
summary: Spontaneous-fission lifetimes are computed as imaginary-time tunnelling along least-action paths in a multidimensional collective space, an instanton/WKB calculation with a coordinate-dependent inertia.
sources: Schunck & Robledo (2016). "Microscopic theory of nuclear fission: a review". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 79, 116301. [arXiv:1511.07517](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.07517)

name: Large scattering length: pionless EFT and cold atoms
summary: Pionless EFT for nucleons and the effective theory of Feshbach-tuned atoms share universal large-scattering-length physics: shallow dimers (deuteron), the three-body parameter and Efimov-like states in nuclei and halos.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)

name: Entanglement entropy in deep inelastic scattering
summary: The parton distribution probed at small x has been interpreted as the entanglement entropy between the probed region and the rest of the proton, linking DIS multiplicities to quantum information.
sources: Kharzeev & Levin (2017). "Deep inelastic scattering as a probe of entanglement". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 114008. [arXiv:1702.03489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03489)

name: Hoyle state as an alpha-particle condensate
summary: The 7.65 MeV Hoyle state of carbon-12 that enables triple-alpha burning has been described as a dilute gas of alpha clusters occupying one orbital, a nuclear analogue of a Bose condensate.
breaks: Only three or four bosons with Pauli effects among constituent nucleons; the condensate fraction is model dependent and debated.
sources: Tohsaki, Horiuchi, Schuck & Röpke (2001). "Alpha Cluster Condensation in 12C and 16O". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 87, 192501. [arXiv:nucl-th/0110014](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0110014)

name: Cold-atom analogues of colour superfluidity
summary: Three-component Fermi gases with attractive interactions can form colour-superfluid and trion ('baryon') phases, an analogue of colour superconductivity and confinement in the dense QCD phase diagram.
breaks: No gauge field or gluon dynamics; trion formation is not confinement; densities map only qualitatively.

name: Photon-counting detectors shared with radiation detection
summary: Scintillation and gamma spectroscopy rely on single-photon-sensitive photodetectors (PMTs, SiPMs), while transition-edge-sensor microcalorimeters developed for quantum optics give eV resolution for gamma and X-ray lines.

name: Laser-trapped radioactive atoms for weak-interaction tests
summary: Magneto-optical and dipole traps hold short-lived radioactive atoms nearly at rest, so recoiling nuclei and beta-neutrino angular correlations can be measured cleanly to search for scalar and tensor weak currents.

name: Odd-even pairing effects in nuclei and SC islands
summary: Small superconducting islands show an even-odd ground-state energy difference from an unpaired quasiparticle, the same blocking effect behind nuclear odd-even mass staggering; quasiparticle poisoning of charge qubits is its device consequence.
map: \Delta E_{\rm odd-even}\approx\Delta\ (\text{gap});\ E_{\rm odd}-E_{\rm even}=\Delta-k_BT\ln N_{\rm eff}

name: Cold atoms as analog Hubbard simulators
summary: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Bose- and Fermi-Hubbard models with tunable U/t, giving clean, disorder-free access to Mott physics and magnetism that motivate condensed-matter questions.
sources: Bloch, Dalibard & Zwerger (2008). "Many-body physics with ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 885. [arXiv:0704.3011](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3011)

name: Superfluid-Mott transition in optical lattices
summary: Deep optical lattices map exactly onto the Bose-Hubbard model; tuning lattice depth drove the superfluid-Mott insulator quantum phase transition, and quantum gas microscopes now image Hubbard correlations site by site.
sources: Jaksch et al. (1998). "Cold Bosonic Atoms in Optical Lattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 81, 3108. [arXiv:cond-mat/9805329](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9805329)
Greiner et al. (2002). "Quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a gas of ultracold atoms". *Nature* 415, 39. [doi:10.1038/415039a](https://doi.org/10.1038/415039a)

name: Quantum simulation of correlated-electron problems
summary: Strongly correlated electron problems (doped Hubbard, pseudogap, stripes) that resist numerics are posed to cold-atom simulators, whose measurements now benchmark DMFT, DMRG and QMC.
sources: Bloch, Dalibard & Zwerger (2008). "Many-body physics with ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 885. [arXiv:0704.3011](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3011)

name: BEC-BCS crossover connects pairs and condensates
summary: Feshbach-tuned Fermi gases cross continuously from BCS Cooper pairing to a BEC of tightly bound molecules; the same gap and number equations describe superconductors at weak coupling.
sources: Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer (1957). "Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 108, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175)
Regal, Greiner & Jin (2004). "Observation of Resonance Condensation of Fermionic Atom Pairs". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 92, 040403. [arXiv:cond-mat/0401554](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0401554)

name: Floquet topological insulators
summary: Periodic driving (circularly polarized light) opens topological gaps in trivial bands; Floquet bands carry Chern and anomalous winding invariants beyond static classification.
sources: Kitagawa et al. (2010). "Topological characterization of periodically driven quantum systems". *Phys. Rev. B* 82, 235114. [arXiv:1010.6126](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.6126)
Lindner, Refael & Galitski (2011). "Floquet topological insulator in semiconductor quantum wells". *Nature Phys.* 7, 490. [arXiv:1008.1792](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.1792)

name: Topological quantum computation with anyons
summary: Braiding non-Abelian anyons of a topologically ordered phase implements gates protected by topology, turning a condensed-matter phase into a quantum computer architecture.
sources: Nayak et al. (2008). "Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1083. [arXiv:0707.1889](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1889)
Kitaev (2003). "Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons". *Ann. Phys.* 303, 2. [arXiv:quant-ph/9707021](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021)

name: Toric code is a topologically ordered phase
summary: The surface/toric code Hamiltonian is a Z2 topologically ordered phase: logical operators are anyon loops, code distance is system size, and the threshold maps to a disorder phase transition of a random-bond Ising model.
sources: Kitaev (2003). "Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons". *Ann. Phys.* 303, 2. [arXiv:quant-ph/9707021](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021)
Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl & Preskill (2002). "Topological quantum memory". *J. Math. Phys.* 43, 4452. [arXiv:quant-ph/0110143](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0110143)

name: Josephson junction as the nonlinear qubit element
summary: The dissipationless nonlinear inductance of a Josephson junction is what makes superconducting circuits anharmonic and hence usable as qubits.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Transmon Hamiltonian from Josephson physics
summary: A capacitively shunted Josephson junction is a quantum pendulum; at E_J/E_C ~ 50 the charge dispersion is exponentially suppressed, giving the transmon qubit.
sources: Koch et al. (2007). "Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box". *Phys. Rev. A* 76, 042319. [arXiv:cond-mat/0703002](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0703002)

name: Superconductors as the material base of qubits
summary: Superconducting qubits inherit BCS physics: the gap protects against dissipation, while quasiparticles, two-level defects and surface oxides of Nb/Al/Ta set coherence.
sources: Clarke & Wilhelm (2008). "Superconducting quantum bits". *Nature* 453, 1031. [doi:10.1038/nature07128](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature07128)

name: Gate-defined quantum-dot spin qubits
summary: Single electrons confined in gate-defined quantum dots carry spin qubits controlled by exchange (Loss-DiVincenzo); Coulomb blockade and charge sensing come from mesoscopic quantum-dot physics.
sources: Loss & DiVincenzo (1998). "Quantum computation with quantum dots". *Phys. Rev. A* 57, 120. [arXiv:cond-mat/9701055](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9701055)

name: 2D materials as hosts for spin and valley qubits
summary: Graphene and TMD quantum dots offer weak hyperfine coupling and valley degrees of freedom as alternative qubit hosts.
sources: Trauzettel, Bulaev, Loss & Burkard (2007). "Spin qubits in graphene quantum dots". *Nature Phys.* 3, 192. [arXiv:cond-mat/0611252](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0611252)

name: Quantum-dot single-photon sources
summary: Self-assembled semiconductor quantum dots are two-level emitters that, embedded in micropillars, give bright, pure and indistinguishable single photons.
sources: Michler et al. (2000). "A Quantum Dot Single-Photon Turnstile Device". *Science* 290, 2282. [doi:10.1126/science.290.5500.2282](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.290.5500.2282)

name: Quantum emitters in 2D semiconductors
summary: Strain- and defect-localized excitons in monolayer WSe2 act as single-photon emitters, linking 2D-material excitonics to quantum-optical sources.
sources: Srivastava et al. (2015). "Optically active quantum dots in monolayer WSe2". *Nature Nanotechnol.* 10, 491. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2015.60](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2015.60)

name: Spin angular momentum as a transport degree of freedom
summary: Spintronics transports and manipulates spin angular momentum: spin precession, spin-orbit coupling (Rashba/Dresselhaus) and spin-transfer torque are the quantum mechanics of spin applied to devices.
map: \dot{\mathbf S}=\gamma\mathbf S\times\mathbf B;\ H_R=\alpha(\boldsymbol\sigma\times\mathbf k)\cdot\hat z
sources: Žutić, Fabian & Das Sarma (2004). "Spintronics: Fundamentals and applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 76, 323. [arXiv:cond-mat/0405528](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0405528)

name: Chern number is integrated Berry curvature
summary: The Hall conductance of a filled band equals the Brillouin-zone integral of Berry curvature (TKNN); geometric-phase concepts define all band-topological invariants.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

Thouless, Kohmoto, Nightingale & den Nijs (1982). "Quantized Hall Conductance in a Two-Dimensional Periodic Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405)
Xiao, Chang & Niu (2010). "Berry phase effects on electronic properties". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1959. [arXiv:0907.2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2021)

name: Geometric phases organize topological matter
summary: Berry's 1984 phase gave condensed matter a unified language for polarization, anomalous Hall effects and topological phases.
sources: Xiao, Chang & Niu (2010). "Berry phase effects on electronic properties". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1959. [arXiv:0907.2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2021)

name: Emergent electromagnetism of skyrmions
summary: Electrons adiabatically following a skyrmion texture acquire a real-space Berry phase that acts as an emergent magnetic flux of one quantum per skyrmion, giving the topological Hall effect.
sources: Nagaosa & Tokura (2013). "Topological properties and dynamics of magnetic skyrmions". *Nature Nanotechnol.* 8, 899. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2013.243](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2013.243)

name: Phonons as qubit resource and error source
summary: Qubits couple coherently to bulk and surface-acoustic phonon modes (quantum acoustodynamics), while phonon bursts from cosmic rays break Cooper pairs and cause chip-wide correlated errors.
sources: Chu et al. (2017). "Quantum acoustics with superconducting qubits". *Science* 358, 199. [arXiv:1703.00342](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00342)
McEwen et al. (2022). "Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits". *Nature Phys.* 18, 107. [arXiv:2104.05219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05219)

name: Planckian dissipation and the chaos bound
summary: Strange metals relax at the Planckian rate hbar/tau ~ k_BT, the same scale as the quantum chaos bound; SYK-type models realize both maximal chaos and linear-in-T resistivity.
sources: Hartnoll (2015). "Theory of universal incoherent metallic transport". *Nature Phys.* 11, 54. [arXiv:1405.3651](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3651)
Li et al. (2024). "Strange Metal and Superconductor in the Two-Dimensional Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 133, 186502. [arXiv:2406.07608](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07608)

name: Preformed pairs and the BEC-BCS crossover
summary: Short coherence lengths in cuprates place them between BCS and BEC limits; the pseudogap has been compared to preformed pairs above T_c in the cold-atom crossover.
breaks: Cuprate pairing is d-wave in a doped Mott insulator with competing orders; the cold-atom crossover is s-wave in a clean continuum gas.
sources: Randeria & Taylor (2014). "Crossover from Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer to Bose-Einstein Condensation and the Unitary Fermi Gas". *Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 5, 209. [arXiv:1306.5785](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5785)

name: Anyon statistics as Berry phases
summary: Exchanging two quasiparticles adiabatically gives a Berry phase; for Laughlin quasiholes it equals pi times the filling, so fractional statistics is a geometric phase.
sources: Arovas, Schrieffer & Wilczek (1984). "Fractional Statistics and the Quantum Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 53, 722. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.722](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.722)

name: Non-Abelian anyons in fractional quantum Hall states
summary: The nu=5/2 state is a candidate Moore-Read phase with Ising anyons; interferometry and braiding there are a proposed route to topological qubits.
sources: Nayak et al. (2008). "Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1083. [arXiv:0707.1889](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1889)

name: Synthetic spin-orbit coupling in quantum gases
summary: Raman dressing gives atoms Rashba/Dresselhaus-like spin-orbit coupling, emulating spintronic Hamiltonians in clean, tunable neutral gases.
breaks: Neutral atoms carry no charge current; synthetic SOC comes with heating from spontaneous emission.
sources: Lin, Jiménez-García & Spielman (2011). "Spin–orbit-coupled Bose–Einstein condensates". *Nature* 471, 83. [arXiv:1103.3522](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3522)

name: Moire materials as solid-state quantum simulators
summary: Twisted bilayers realize tunable lattice models (triangular Hubbard, flat Chern bands) by twist angle and gating, playing the role optical lattices play for atoms.
breaks: Moire electrons have long-range Coulomb interactions, phonons and disorder; filling and interactions are tuned differently from cold atoms.
sources: Kennes et al. (2021). "Moiré heterostructures as a condensed-matter quantum simulator". *Nature Phys.* 17, 155. [arXiv:2011.12638](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.12638)

name: Electron quantum optics
summary: Single-electron sources, quantum point contacts as beam splitters and edge channels as waveguides let electronic HOM and HBT experiments mirror photon statistics; shot noise is the fermionic g2.
sources: Bocquillon et al. (2013). "Coherence and Indistinguishability of Single Electrons Emitted by Independent Sources". *Science* 339, 1054. [doi:10.1126/science.1232572](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1232572)

name: Exciton and polariton condensation
summary: Excitons and exciton-polaritons are composite bosons that condense at high temperature because of their light mass; interlayer TMD excitons are candidate equilibrium exciton condensates.
sources: Kasprzak et al. (2006). "Bose–Einstein condensation of exciton polaritons". *Nature* 443, 409. [doi:10.1038/nature05131](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature05131)

name: Strong coupling of excitons to cavity photons
summary: Excitons in microcavities reach strong coupling, forming polaritons with vacuum Rabi splitting, the Jaynes-Cummings physics of cavity QED with a collective emitter.
sources: Kasprzak et al. (2006). "Bose–Einstein condensation of exciton polaritons". *Nature* 443, 409. [doi:10.1038/nature05131](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature05131)

name: Quasiparticles limit qubit coherence
summary: Non-equilibrium Bogoliubov quasiparticles above the BCS gap tunnel across junctions and cause relaxation and parity switching; gap engineering and phonon traps suppress them.

name: Macroscopic quantum tunnelling in Josephson junctions
summary: Caldeira and Leggett's theory of dissipative tunnelling and the 1985 observation of quantized levels in a current-biased junction showed a macroscopic phase variable obeys quantum mechanics (Nobel 2025).
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Quantum tunnelling in a dissipative system". *Ann. Phys.* 149, 374. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(83)90202-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(83)90202-6)

Martinis, Devoret & Clarke (1985). "Energy-Level Quantization in the Zero-Voltage State of a Current-Biased Josephson Junction". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 55, 1543. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1543](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1543)

name: Fermi-Hubbard simulators target cuprate physics
summary: Quantum gas microscopes observed long-range antiferromagnetism and then hole-doped correlations in the 2D Fermi-Hubbard model, addressing the doped-Mott-insulator physics of cuprates.
sources: Mazurenko et al. (2017). "A cold-atom Fermi–Hubbard antiferromagnet". *Nature* 545, 462. [arXiv:1612.08436](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08436)

name: Bloch bands in optical lattices
summary: Atoms in optical lattices obey Bloch's theorem with tight-binding bands and Wannier functions; Bloch oscillations, unobservable in solids because of scattering, are seen directly.
sources: Ben Dahan et al. (1996). "Bloch Oscillations of Atoms in an Optical Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 76, 4508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.4508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.4508)

name: Superexchange observed with cold atoms
summary: In optical double wells, second-order tunnelling produces superexchange J=4t^2/U between spins, measured in real time.
sources: Trotzky et al. (2008). "Time-Resolved Observation and Control of Superexchange Interactions with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices". *Science* 319, 295. [arXiv:0712.1853](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1853)

name: Rydberg arrays realize a Z2 spin liquid
summary: Rydberg-blockade atom arrays on a ruby lattice prepared a state with topological string order of a Z2 quantum spin liquid, a phase long sought in frustrated magnets.
sources: Semeghini et al. (2021). "Probing topological spin liquids on a programmable quantum simulator". *Science* 374, 1242. [arXiv:2104.04119](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04119)

name: Topological entanglement entropy
summary: Topological order leaves a universal negative constant in the entanglement entropy area law, set by the total quantum dimension of the anyons.
sources: Kitaev & Preskill (2006). "Topological Entanglement Entropy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110404. [arXiv:hep-th/0510092](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0510092)
Levin & Wen (2006). "Detecting Topological Order in a Ground State Wave Function". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110405. [arXiv:cond-mat/0510613](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0510613)

name: Area laws make DMRG and tensor networks work
summary: Gapped ground states obey entanglement area laws, so matrix-product states with bounded bond dimension represent them faithfully; DMRG is variational optimization over MPS.
sources: White (1992). "Density matrix formulation for quantum renormalization groups". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 69, 2863. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863)
Hastings (2007). "An area law for one-dimensional quantum systems". *J. Stat. Mech.* 0708, P08024. [arXiv:0705.2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.2024)

name: Quantum algorithms for correlated materials
summary: Phase estimation, VQE and Hamiltonian simulation target ground states and dynamics of Hubbard-type models that classical numerics cannot reach, the leading candidate for quantum advantage.
sources: Bauer, Bravyi, Motta & Chan (2020). "Quantum Algorithms for Quantum Chemistry and Quantum Materials Science". *Chem. Rev.* 120, 12685. [arXiv:2001.03685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.03685)

name: Bulk Fermi arcs from exceptional points
summary: Finite quasiparticle lifetimes make the effective Hamiltonian non-Hermitian; Weyl or Dirac nodes split into exceptional rings joined by bulk Fermi arcs.
sources: Kozii & Fu (2024). "Non-Hermitian topological theory of finite-lifetime quasiparticles: Prediction of bulk Fermi arc due to exceptional point". [arXiv:1708.05841](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05841)

name: Non-Hermitian band topology
summary: Gain and loss extend band topology to point and line gaps; spectral winding gives the skin effect and modifies bulk-boundary correspondence, enlarging the tenfold classification.
sources: Gong et al. (2018). "Topological Phases of Non-Hermitian Systems". *Phys. Rev. X* 8, 031079. [arXiv:1802.07964](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07964)

name: Light-induced anomalous Hall effect in graphene
summary: Circularly polarized light opens a Floquet gap at graphene's Dirac points; an anomalous Hall response was measured in ultrafast transport.
sources: Oka & Aoki (2009). "Photovoltaic Hall effect in graphene". *Phys. Rev. B* 79, 081406. [arXiv:0807.4767](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.4767)
McIver et al. (2020). "Light-induced anomalous Hall effect in graphene". *Nature Phys.* 16, 38. [arXiv:1811.03522](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.03522)

name: Chern bands and Hofstadter models with cold atoms
summary: Shaken and laser-assisted-tunnelling optical lattices realized the Haldane and Harper-Hofstadter models, measuring Chern numbers of synthetic quantum-Hall bands.
sources: Jotzu et al. (2014). "Experimental realization of the topological Haldane model with ultracold fermions". *Nature* 515, 237. [arXiv:1406.7874](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7874)
Aidelsburger et al. (2013). "Realization of the Hofstadter Hamiltonian with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 111, 185301. [arXiv:1308.0321](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0321)

name: Exchange from spin algebra and Pauli exclusion
summary: Heisenberg exchange arises because the Coulomb energy depends on the singlet or triplet spin state through antisymmetry; addition of spin angular momenta gives the S1.S2 form.

name: Weyl points as Berry-curvature monopoles
summary: Berry's degeneracy monopole is realized in crystals: Weyl nodes are sources of Berry flux with integer charge, giving Fermi arcs and the chiral anomaly.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

Wan et al. (2011). "Topological semimetal and Fermi-arc surface states in the electronic structure of pyrochlore iridates". *Phys. Rev. B* 83, 205101. [arXiv:1007.0016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0016)

name: Berry phase pi of graphene's Dirac electrons
summary: Pseudospin winding gives graphene electrons a pi Berry phase, producing the half-integer quantum Hall sequence and suppressed backscattering.
sources: Zhang, Tan, Stormer & Kim (2005). "Experimental observation of the quantum Hall effect and Berry's phase in graphene". *Nature* 438, 201. [arXiv:cond-mat/0509355](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0509355)

name: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in mesoscopic rings
summary: Phase-coherent electrons in metal rings show conductance oscillations with flux period h/e, a direct transport measurement of the Aharonov-Bohm phase.
sources: Webb et al. (1985). "Observation of h/e Aharonov-Bohm Oscillations in Normal-Metal Rings". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 54, 2696. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.2696](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.2696)

name: Majorana zero modes as topological qubits
summary: Majorana zero modes at Kitaev-chain ends store a qubit in nonlocal fermion parity; braiding gives protected Clifford gates. Experimental claims in nanowires remain contested.
sources: Kitaev (2001). "Unpaired Majorana fermions in quantum wires". *Phys.-Usp.* 44, 131. [arXiv:cond-mat/0010440](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0010440)
Nayak et al. (2008). "Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1083. [arXiv:0707.1889](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1889)

name: Donor and Si/SiGe spin qubits
summary: Silicon spin qubits rely on semiconductor physics: donor levels, valley splitting, isotopic purification of Si-28 and CMOS fabrication.
sources: Kane (1998). "A silicon-based nuclear spin quantum computer". *Nature* 393, 133. [doi:10.1038/30156](https://doi.org/10.1038/30156)

name: Cavity QED with quantum dots
summary: Single quantum dots in photonic-crystal nanocavities reach strong coupling with vacuum Rabi splitting, the solid-state realization of Jaynes-Cummings physics.
sources: Yoshie et al. (2004). "Vacuum Rabi splitting with a single quantum dot in a photonic crystal nanocavity". *Nature* 432, 200. [doi:10.1038/nature03119](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature03119)

name: Mechanical resonators are engineered phonons
summary: Optomechanical resonators are phonon modes of nanostructures; phononic band gaps, Brillouin scattering and two-level-system damping are lattice-dynamics physics.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: NV magnetometry images electron hydrodynamics
summary: Nitrogen-vacancy centres used as nanoscale quantum magnetometers imaged the Poiseuille flow profile of the Dirac fluid in graphene.
sources: Ku et al. (2020). "Imaging viscous flow of the Dirac fluid in graphene". *Nature* 583, 537. [arXiv:1905.10791](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10791)

name: Nuclear-spin bath decoherence of dot spins
summary: In GaAs dots the electron spin decoheres through hyperfine coupling to ~1e6 nuclear spins, a central-spin model of system-bath decoherence that drove the move to isotopically purified Si.
sources: Khaetskii, Loss & Glazman (2002). "Electron Spin Decoherence in Quantum Dots due to Interaction with Nuclei". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 88, 186802. [arXiv:cond-mat/0201303](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0201303)

name: Kitaev honeycomb model and Kitaev materials
summary: Kitaev's exactly solvable honeycomb model has a Z2 spin-liquid ground state with Majorana excitations; it motivates the search in alpha-RuCl3 and iridates.
sources: Kitaev (2006). "Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond". *Ann. Phys.* 321, 2. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506438](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506438)
